title: From Data to Policy : Strengthening Essential Climate Variable Monitoring with Deep Learning Algorithms and Data Quality Standards
abstract: Essential Climate Variables (ECVs) are critical for understanding and monitoring climate systems, providing important data to assess climate change and supporting policy formulation. This review emphasizes the importance of ensuring data quality, traceability, and consistency to derive reliable features from ECV datasets, addressing challenges such as temporal and spatial coverage gaps, calibration discrepancies, and harmonization across diverse sources. Furthermore, we highlight both the transformative potential and limits of advanced analytics, including artificial intelligence (AI), in enhancing the monitoring and prediction of ECVs using three case studies: (i) climate modeling and prediction of temperatures for planning scenario with machine learning, (ii) the Earth’s surface processes, and (iii) monitoring the Earth radiation budget. This article also explores how ECVs are integrated into global frameworks like the Global Climate Observing System (GCOS) and the WMO Integrated Global Observing System (WIGOS), which establish standardized protocols for reliable and interoperable data. By synthesizing advances in technology, data quality practices, and global collaboration efforts, this review underscores the importance of interdisciplinary approaches to bridge the gap between scientific knowledge and actionable climate policies.
problem: Deriving reliable and actionable features from Essential Climate Variable (ECV) datasets for policy-making is hindered by challenges like temporal/spatial gaps, calibration discrepancies, and inconsistent data quality, which undermine the traceability and consistency required for robust climate monitoring and modeling.
method: This paper proposes strengthening Essential Climate Variable (ECV) monitoring by systematically combining deep learning algorithms with rigorous data quality standards to enhance the scientific utility and policy relevance of climate data.
task: The task is to review how deep learning algorithms and data quality standards can strengthen the monitoring of Essential Climate Variables (ECVs) to bridge the gap between scientific data and actionable climate policies.

On the incoming side, the Total Solar Irradiance (TSI), the spectrally integrated energy at a distance of 1 AU from the Sun, is measured at the Top Of the Earth's Atmosphere (TOA). TSI measurements started in 1978 using numerous space instruments [116], [117]. For more than 30 years, the challenge was that the calibration uncertainty of the TSI radiometers with respect to the official international standards for measurement was large (> 0.35%) compared the solar cycle variability (0.1%) and expected Earth Energy Imbalance (EEI) (approx. 0.04% of the TSI), making it a) difficult to concatenate the measurements from different satellites and b) impossible to estimate the EEI.

W. Finsterle is a senior scientist and the head of the World Standard Group (WSG) at PMOD/WRC. He has more than 30 years of experience in radiometry. He is the PI of the PMO6 radiometer on board of the SOHO/VIRGO mission, the PI of the DARA instrument on the FY3E/JTSIM mission, the PI of the CLARA/NORSAT-1 absolute radiometer and the co-PI of the DARA-PROBA3 radiometer on the ESA-PROBA3 satellite (expected to be launched later in 2024).
